hero.subtitle: When a hospital visit or procedure in Truckee goes wrong, sorting out what happened can feel overwhelming on top of Nevada County's limited local specialty care. We provide a free case review and can help you understand California's medical malpractice rules.

about.title: Truckee Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Truckee residents and the many visitors who pass through this Nevada County mountain town sometimes rely on urgent care clinics, small hospitals, or specialists located down the hill in Reno or Sacramento for serious treatment. When distance, rushed diagnoses, or communication gaps between providers lead to a preventable injury, it's worth having the situation reviewed. California's medical malpractice law, known as MICRA, sets specific rules around how long you have to act, what notice must be given before filing, and how damages are calculated — a bad medical outcome by itself doesn't automatically mean malpractice occurred. We handle medical malpractice cases and can evaluate your medical records, consult with a qualified expert if needed, and explain your options. There's no cost for an initial review, and we are paid only if your case results in a recovery. Reaching out early matters, since strict deadlines apply.

Failure to recognize a worsening emergency condition

whyChoose.title: What Makes Truckee Malpractice Claims Different

items.title: Strict, Layered Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, but never more than three years from the injury itself. A 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider is also required before a lawsuit can move forward.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a poor result doesn't automatically prove negligence, California law nearly always requires a qualified medical expert to review the care and confirm it fell below the accepted standard.

items.title: Damages Caps That Change Yearly
items.desc: California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages in these cases, and that cap rises each year by law. We can walk you through how this affects your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Truckee?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, but no more than three years from when it happened. A 90-day written notice to the healthcare provider is also required before filing suit. Because these deadlines can overlap in confusing ways, it's best to have us review your timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: Does a bad outcome from surgery or treatment automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law requires proof that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, and a qualified medical expert almost always has to confirm that. A disappointing or painful result isn't, by itself, evidence of negligence.

items.question: I was treated at a small Truckee clinic before being transferred elsewhere — does that complicate my claim?
items.answer: It can add a layer of review since multiple providers and possibly multiple facilities may be involved, especially given how often patients here are transferred to larger hospitals in Reno or Sacramento. We can help sort out which provider's actions are relevant and gather the right records from each location.
